summary: After the Braves beat the Phillies 5-4 in NLDS Game 2, Fox Sports' Jake Mintz reported that Braves shortstop Orlando Arcia taunted Bryce Harper in the clubhouse by yelling "Atta boy Harper." The comment motivated Harper, who homered twice in Game 3, and became a Phillies rallying cry after they eliminated Atlanta. MLB Network's Alanna Rizzo blasted Mintz on air, drawing backlash from journalists and a BBWAA statement, and she then apologized publicly and privately.
one_line: Orlando Arcia's clubhouse taunt of Bryce Harper, reported by Jake Mintz, sparked a reporting-ethics row and Alanna Rizzo's on-air attack and apology.
key_facts: The Braves beat the Phillies 5-4 in Game 2 of the NLDS, ending on a play in which Bryce Harper was doubled off after Michael Harris robbed Nick Castellanos of a hit.

Fox Sports' Jake Mintz, one of the two brothers behind the Cespedes Family BBQ account, reported that Orlando Arcia repeatedly yelled "ha-ha, atta-boy, Harper!" in the Braves' clubhouse as reporters circled the room.
Harper homered twice in the Phillies' 10-2 Game 3 win, staring down Arcia after each home run.
After the Phillies beat the Braves in Game 4 to advance to the NLCS, Philadelphia players celebrated in the clubhouse by repeating "Atta boy Harper."
Blue Jays pitcher Kevin Gausman was among players who said Mintz was wrong to report comments made out loud in a locker room rather than in an interview.
MLB Network's Alanna Rizzo blasted Mintz on "High Heat," saying "this guy, Jake Mintz, that's not even a reporter" and calling the clubhouse "a sacred space."

The Washington Post's Chelsea Janes also wrote about the yelling but did not name the player, and later defended Mintz, saying cameras and recorders were running with more than a dozen reporters present.
Janes said that not reporting Arcia's comments would be "protecting players from themselves" and that the Braves should win if they don't want it to be the story.
The BBWAA defended Mintz as a member in good standing and said it was "deeply troubled" that MLB's own network allowed him to be disparaged.
Rizzo apologized on "High Heat" and privately to Mintz, calling her comments "completely inappropriate" and "beyond unprofessional."
Mintz called her initial comments "incredibly hurtful/uncalled for" but said he was "glad she apologized" and asked people not to send her hate.
In Game 2, Austin Riley scooped Harris' errant throw and threw to Matt Olson to nab Harper at first and end the game.
